newsitem.title: BELGIUM: King urges truth on paedophile protection charges.
newsitem.headline: King urges truth on paedophile protection charges.

text.p: Belgium's King Albert told his people on Sunday that no stone should be left unturned in finding out whether the culprits in a child murder and sex scandal which rocked the country got high-level protection.

Addressing Belgians for their national day on Monday, the king said it was essential that a special parliamentary commission investigating the scandal "should go right to the end into the question of eventual protection."
He was referring to growing allegations of official protection for Marc Dutroux, who is alleged to have murdered four children and imprisoned and sexually abused two others.

In a speech aimed at raising morale after a year which also brought revelations of large-scale corruption in Belgium's political party system, King Albert said the crises had brought about "a will for change, which is already starting to bear fruit."

A quarter of a million people took to the streets last October for a "white march" in support of the parents of the child sex scandal and in protest at what they saw as a corrupt and morally bankrupt justice system.

"Let's avoid falling into a climate of generalised suspicion. The road will be long. It is a question not only of reforming institutions but also and above all of mentalities and behaviour," the king said.
Last year's grisly paedophilia saga was unleashed when two sexually-abused young girls were rescued from a makeshift dungeon in the house of Dutroux, a convicted child rapist.
Within days police dug up the bodies of two eight-year-old girls in another of his houses and later unearthed the bodies of two teenage girls in the grounds of a property linked to him.
The special parliamentary commission has increasingly focused on allegations that Dutroux, who has been charged with the murder of all four girls, enjoyed official protection.
In March this year the body of a fifth girl, aged nine when she disappeared in August 1992, was found in a steel trunk in the basement of a Brussels garage.
Patrick Derochette, a convicted child molester who worked for the garage, has been charged with the abduction, rape of a child under 10 and illegal imprisonment leading to death.
King Albert said it was also essential for the Belgian justice system to throw light on inquiries still going on into missing children.
